records.publicLabel: Clean Slate erasure for offenses from 2000 onward

retainedBStage.identity: State agencies identify and erase eligible post-2000 convictions through the Clean Slate data process.
retainedBStage.selectorDescription: Select the retained stage when the conviction was entered on or after January 1, 2000, is in the automatic cohort, and needs no participant filing to initiate erasure.
retainedBStage.outputStrategyDescription: Provide non-filing status, verification, and correction-escalation guidance; do not generate a participant filing.
retainedBStage.productOutcomeDescription: The participant receives an explanation of the automatic stage and how to verify whether the state completed erasure.

commercialTreatment.description: The automatic stage is never a participant-fileable or sellable route.

participantABranch.identity: Participant review or petition branch for a missed automatic erasure or an eligible pre-2000 conviction.
participantABranch.selectorDescription: Select the participant branch when an eligible post-2000 conviction remains unerased after it should have been erased, or when the otherwise eligible conviction predates January 1, 2000.
participantABranch.outputStrategyDescription: Reuse the existing JD-CR-202 official-PDF route and carry SPBI-supported DESPP review and hearing-request guidance with it; stop before a contested hearing or judicial review.
participantABranch.productOutcomeDescription: The participant receives the existing JD-CR-202 filing route plus SPBI-supported DESPP review and hearing-request guidance. A contested hearing or judicial review requires professional handoff and is not delivered by this branch.

commercialTreatment.description: Legacy runtime capability does not grant current commercial authority. The branch remains closed unless an exact Grade-A fulfillment record later authorizes this route and packet family.

participantABranch.filingActor: The person whose conviction is involved, or counsel.

instruments.name: Application to DESPP for review of a conviction that should have been automatically erased
instruments.purpose: Initiates agency review. If the dispute proceeds to a contested hearing or judicial review, the participant stops for professional help.

instruments.name: Petition for Clean Slate Erasure
instruments.purpose: Files the qualifying pre-2000 petition and is the named official form bound to the existing Category A route.

supportingEvidence.name: SPBI criminal-history record check
supportingEvidence.purpose: Documents a conviction that should have been erased and supports the missed-erasure hearing request.

destinations: DESPP/State Police for review of a missed automatic erasure
Superior Court, G.A. location of sentencing, for JD-CR-202
participantABranch.trigger: An eligible post-2000 conviction remains unerased after the automatic process should have completed, or an otherwise eligible conviction predates January 1, 2000.
participantABranch.deadline: No fixed calendar filing deadline is stated in the committed record. Missed-erasure review becomes available after the record should have been erased; agency hearing and decision timing follows Conn. Gen. Stat. § 54-142t. For JD-CR-202, the waiting period is seven years for a qualifying misdemeanor or ten years for a qualifying felony, measured from the person's most recent conviction for any crime; the entire sentence, including all supervision, must also be complete.
